name.text: GAIMS V1 - Plant Operator: Rankine cycle design point

questiontext.text:
(5 points) You are commissioning the steam cycle of a condensing power plant. The Plant Operator simulator for your assigned unit is linked above; open it and enter your instance code before answering.

Your unit operates on an ideal-component Rankine cycle with real turbomachinery:

  • Boiler exit (turbine inlet): 8 MPa, 480 °C
  • Condenser pressure: 10 kPa, with saturated liquid leaving the condenser
  • Turbine isentropic efficiency: ηt = {eta_t}
  • Pump isentropic efficiency: ηp = {eta_p}
  • Required net power output: {Wnet} MW
  • Turbine-exit moisture limit: steam quality must not fall below xmin = {xmin}

Work with the state values shown in the simulator's state-point table. Give all answers to at least three significant figures.

{#1}

{#2}

{#3}

{#4}

{#5}

generalfeedback.text:
Method. Pump: \( w_p = v_1 (P_2 - P_1)/\eta_p \), so \( h_2 = h_1 + w_p \). Turbine: \( x_{4s} = (s_3 - s_f)/s_{fg} \), \( h_{4s} = h_f + x_{4s} h_{fg} \), \( w_t = \eta_t (h_3 - h_{4s}) \), so \( h_4 = h_3 - w_t \). Then \( q_{in} = h_3 - h_2 \), \( w_{net} = w_t - w_p \), \( \eta_{th} = w_{net}/q_{in} \), \( x_4 = (h_4 - h_f)/h_{fg} \) and \( \dot m = \dot W_{net}/w_{net} \).

Why the moisture limit matters. A higher turbine isentropic efficiency raises \( w_t \) and therefore lowers \( h_4 \) and \( x_4 \). The design point that maximises efficiency is not necessarily admissible: check \( x_4 \) against your unit's \( x_{min} = {xmin} \) before recommending it. Your unit's computed exit quality is {x4}, and the limit is {xmin}.

Pump work. Note that \( w_p \) is small but not zero here; discarding it changes \( \eta_{th} \) in the third significant figure, which is inside the grading tolerance for this question but not inside the tolerance of a real acceptance test.

correctfeedback.text: All four quantities are correct for your unit.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some quantities are correct for your unit. Check the parts marked incorrect against your state-point table.

incorrectfeedback.text: None of the quantities match your unit's operating point. Re-read the state-point table in the simulator before trying again.

subqtext.text:
(1 point) Cycle thermal efficiency, as a decimal fraction (not a percentage), including pump work.

\( \eta_{th} \) = {_0}

feedback.text: Use \( \eta_{th} = w_{net}/q_{in} \) with \( q_{in} = h_3 - h_2 \). A common error is to use \( h_3 - h_1 \), which ignores the pump's enthalpy rise.

subqtext.text:
(1 point) Net specific work delivered by the cycle. Include the unit.

\( w_{net} \) = {_0}

feedback.text: \( w_{net} = w_t - w_p \). The pump term is small, but it is not zero: at your pump efficiency it is roughly {wp} kJ/kg.

subqtext.text:
(1 point) Steam quality at the actual turbine exit, as a decimal fraction. Then compare it with your unit's limit \( x_{min} = {xmin} \) — you will be asked to justify the comparison in the linked Workshop activity.

\( x_4 \) = {_0}

feedback.text: Use the actual exit enthalpy \( h_4 = h_3 - w_t \), not the isentropic \( h_{4s} \). Irreversibility in the turbine raises \( h_4 \) and therefore raises the exit quality relative to the isentropic case.

subqtext.text:
(1 point) Steam mass flow rate required to deliver the specified net output of {Wnet} MW. Include the unit.

\( \dot m \) = {_0}

feedback.text: \( \dot m = \dot W_{net} / w_{net} \). Watch the unit conversion: the required output is given in MW and the specific work in kJ/kg.

subqtext.text:
(1 point) Actual specific work consumed by the feed pump, at your unit's pump isentropic efficiency ηp = {eta_p}. Include the unit. Then state, in the Workshop activity, what percentage of gross turbine work this represents.

\( w_p \) = {_0}

feedback.text: Treat the liquid as incompressible: \( w_{p,s} = v_1 (P_2 - P_1) \), and divide by \( \eta_p \) for the actual work. Note that \( 1\ \mathrm{kPa \cdot m^3/kg} = 1\ \mathrm{kJ/kg} \), so no further conversion is needed. The magnitude is small — but your unit's \( \eta_p \) changes it by around 20% across the class, which is why it is graded separately.

hint.text: Start from the four state points. State 1 is saturated liquid at the condenser pressure; state 3 is the turbine inlet. You need \( h_2 \) and \( h_4 \) before any of the four answers.
For the turbine, find the isentropic exit state first: \( s_{4s} = s_3 \), so \( x_{4s} = (s_3 - s_f)/s_{fg} \). Apply \( \eta_t \) to the isentropic enthalpy drop, not to the enthalpy itself.
If your efficiency is high but your exit quality is below {xmin}, the design point is inadmissible for your unit — that is the constraint the simulator's shaded region is showing you.
